chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the prayer of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله by day, so he said: “And who can manage that?” Then he said: “But shall I not inform you how I myself act?” So I said: Yes.

He said: “Eight rak'ahs before al-Zuhr and eight after it.” I said: And al-Maghrib? He said: “Four after it.” I said: And al-'Atamah? He said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used to perform al-'Atamah, then sleep.” And he gestured with his hand like this, moving it.
Ibn Abi 'Umayr said: Then he عليه السلام described it as our companions have mentioned.

key_terms.أَصْحَابُنَا: our companions, meaning the transmitters or associates referred to by Ibn Abi 'Umayr
key_terms.الْعَتَمَةُ: the night prayer referred to here in the report
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَ رَكَعَاتٍ: eight units of prayer prescribed here as a recommended practice
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.صَلَاةِ: salat (prayer), here referring to the devotional prayer practice being asked about

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام narrate about the recommended prayers before and after al-Zuhr, al-Maghrib, and al-'Atamah?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a question to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام about the daytime prayer practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. The Imam indicates that the full prophetic practice is difficult to sustain, then explains his own established pattern of recommended prayers around al-Zuhr and al-Maghrib, and mentions that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله would perform al-'Atamah and then sleep.
